**Problem.** Updating a pull request body strips the _Generated by Claude Code_ footer and appends no replacement, so an edit that relied on the server's footer publishes with no attribution at all

**Observed three times on `#901`, 2026-09-22, each write read back.**

1. **Create.** The body sent ended `---` / `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`, then the `🤖 Generated with ...` lines. Published: the `🤖` lines in place, and the `_Generated by_` footer *moved* to the very end with its URL rewritten to carry the session id.
2. **Update.** The body sent ended with the `_Generated by_` footer and no `🤖` lines. Published: **no footer at all.** The server stripped the model-written one as a duplicate and appended none of its own.
3. **Update.** The body sent ended with the `🤖` lines and no `_Generated by_` footer. Published: exactly that, unchanged.

So the rule the writes are consistent with is: a `_Generated by [Claude Code]_`
footer is stripped from the body on *every* write, and the server appends its
own only on **create**. An update that relies on the server to supply it
therefore publishes with no attribution, silently and with a success response.

**Why it matters.** This is the `PL-1DN9` class - the published body differing
from the one sent, with success returned either way - and nothing catches it.
`tools/pr_body_check.py` reports a squash commit that landed with an *empty*
body; a body that landed with its attribution removed is not empty and is
invisible to it. The harness rule that every pull request description carries
the attribution is then satisfiable only by a model that includes the `🤖`
form itself on every update, which no instruction currently says.

**Done when.** The mechanism is confirmed or refuted against a second
repository or a fresh pull request, since one pull request is one sample and
the server's duplicate-footer handling is the only part inferred rather than
observed; and, if confirmed, whichever of these is right: the `🤖` form is
stated as the one to write on an update, or `pr_body_check.py` grows a rule
for an attribution-less body beside the empty-body one it already has. Not
both without a reason - the second costs a check on every session start.

**What it is not.** Not a defect in this repository's code. The write is the
GitHub API through the harness, so the repair here is either an instruction or
a detector, and which of those is worth having is the decision this item holds.
